18.0.s.en: (1) The agreement of Jehoshaphat and Ahab

18.0.0.en: God's blessing on Jehoshaphat continued, so he became very rich, but he thought of relying on the powers of the world, so he made a marriage alliance with Ahab king of Israel, that is, he married his son Jehoram to Athaliah the daughter of Ahab. This was a great mistake, for it was a betrayal of God, who had magnified him greatly, and consequently there was no need to ally himself with a wicked king who worshiped idols, because Ahab was the most wicked of the kings of Israel. This mistake exposed Jehoshaphat to death, but God rescued him for the sake of his goodness, mentioned in the previous chapter, yet it corrupted his kingdom, because the daughter of Ahab brought the worship of idols into the kingdom of Judah; she was a wicked woman and reigned over Judah, and then was killed. Thus we see that Jehoshaphat's wealth made him attached to money and greatness, so he neglected the Law of God and allied himself with idol worshipers. Perhaps Jehoshaphat thought that by his marriage alliance with Ahab he would reach a union of the two kingdoms, but his mistake was that he did not consult God in this matter, so he did not reach union, but corrupted the kingdom of Judah as well.

18.0.1.en: Always thank God for the gifts He has given you, because all the capabilities you have are a gift of God, which He can withdraw from you if you neglect His commandments. As you have abandoned Him, He can abandon you, perhaps that you may repent and not lose your eternity. So why expose yourself to afflictions? Be precise, holding fast to the commandments of God in His Church all your life.

18.1.0.en: Jerusalem was built on hills; therefore it says that Jehoshaphat went down and traveled to Samaria, the capital of the kingdom of Israel, and this was some years after he began to reign, during which he had reached great eminence. Ahab considered this visit very great, so he killed many sacrifices for Jehoshaphat and made a great feast for him and all who were with him. And Ahab took advantage of this opportunity and asked Jehoshaphat to ally with him in fighting the Arameans to recover the city of Ramoth-gilead, which lies east of the Jordan River in the tribe of Gad, and which the Arameans had taken. Perhaps Ahab seduced Jehoshaphat by saying that this alliance between the two kingdoms would benefit them against the surrounding nations, so Jehoshaphat agreed.

19.0.s.en: (1) Jehu the seer's rebuke of Jehoshaphat

19.0.0.en: After Jehoshaphat escaped from his war with the Arameans, in which Ahab died, he fell into another mistake, which was his alliance with Joram king of Israel, the grandson of Ahab, in his war against Moab (2 Kgs 3:7), which is not mentioned in the Book of Chronicles; then after this he returned to Jerusalem in peace, that is, no bodily harm came to him, but he lost his inner peace as a result of his association with the wicked and God's abandoning him.

19.0.1.en: At first sight we understand from this verse that Jehoshaphat, after returning from his war in which he allied with Ahab against the Arameans, returned to Jerusalem; but the truth, as we have explained, is that Jehoshaphat's return to Jerusalem in this verse was after his war in which he allied with Joram against Moab, and we understood this from the following verses, which show God's rebuke of him and his repentance, until the end of his life and his keeping away from alliance with the kingdom of Israel.

19.1.0.en: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer: a prophet, the son of Hanani the seer, who rebuked Asa, and he imprisoned him (ch. 16:10). And Jehu is the one who rebuked Baasha king of Israel (1 Kgs 16:1-4). When Jehoshaphat returned to Jerusalem after his alliance with Ahab, and then with Joram his grandson, Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to him with a rebuke from God, and said to him: How do you help Ahab and Joram his grandson, the wicked, and how dare you love those who hate the Lord, who worshiped idols and rejected God? Therefore, God is angry with you. And this actually happened, because despite Jehoshaphat's repentance, his return to God and his reforms, God's wrath was upon the offspring of Jehoshaphat, that is, his son Jehoram, who walked in evil, for he killed his brothers and the princes of his people; then Athaliah the wife of Jehoram, the son of Jehoshaphat, came and helped her son Ahaziah in evil and reigned after his death, and killed all the royal offspring except Joash, who escaped. And because God accepted Jehoshaphat's repentance and goodness, He did not punish him in his lifetime.

19.1.1.en: We see here God's care for Jehoshaphat: he is a good king, but he slipped into alliance with the wicked, so God did not leave him, but sent him a prophet to rebuke him, so that he would repent.

19.1.2.en: God loves you, even after you sin, and calls you to repentance and rebukes you, or allows afflictions for you so that you return to Him. So may you take heed and return quickly, to regain God's compassion and His care for you.

19.2.0.en: Jehu continued his words to Jehoshaphat and drew him on, saying that God has not forgotten your love for Him and your removal of the worship of idols, that is, the altars and the groves, and your care for the worship of God. We see here God's encouragement of His children, even as He rebukes them, to give them hope of repentance. For despite rebuking Jehoshaphat for his alliance with the wicked, He says to him that there is a good thing in you, which is your love for God and your refusal of the worship of idols.

19.3.0.en: Jehoshaphat submitted to the word of God through Jehu, and repented of his sins, so he stayed in Jerusalem and began to care for the spiritual life of his people. He took care of the people in Jerusalem, then visited all the kingdom of Judah from its south at Beersheba to its north in the mountain of Ephraim, and so we see Jehoshaphat's concern to visit all the cities of his kingdom himself, to bring the people back to God and call them to repentance. Perhaps his preoccupation with the alliance with the kings of Israel made him neglect the care of his people, in addition to the fact that Athaliah the daughter of Ahab, who married Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, was very wicked, and perhaps she spread the worship of idols in Jerusalem and its surroundings. And Jehoshaphat's concern to call his people to repentance is clear evidence of his repentance, and an attempt to repair the effects of his mistakes. As the people were made to stumble because Jehoshaphat mixed with idol worship, so he takes care to call them to repentance.

19.4.0.en: Jehoshaphat had sent princes, priests and Levites to teach the people (ch. 17:7-9), but the people's straying from the Law made Jehoshaphat appoint judges in all the cities of Judah, to judge by the Law of God in all disputes, and to pass sentence on the wrongdoers who refused to return to the Lord; for the number of judges previously existing was small, so out of Jehoshaphat's concern he appointed many judges in every place.

19.5.0.en: Jehoshaphat gave the judges a set of instructions when he sent them to judge the children of Israel, which are:

19.5.1.en: 1- That their work in judging is for God and not for man, and this makes their work of the utmost importance and seriousness, because it is offered to God before it is offered to man, so they must do it with uprightness of heart and all exactness (v. 6).

19.5.2.en: 2- He promised them that God would support them and guide them in every problem and encourage and strengthen them (v. 6).

19.5.3.en: 3- He promised them that God would give them awe in the eyes of the people, so they would respect them and submit to them (v. 7).

19.5.4.en: 4- He warned them not to wrong anyone, or show partiality to anyone, or take a bribe (bribery), for they must be representatives of God, who rejects injustice, partiality and bribery (v. 7).

19.5.5.en: 5- After Jehoshaphat visited the cities of Judah and appointed judges in them (v. 5), he established a high court in Jerusalem of the priests, the Levites and the heads of the fathers, to settle the great disputes, and commanded the judges to refer to the supreme kingdom in everything that was too hard for them to decide in the cities of Judah (v. 8).

19.5.6.en: 6- He commanded them to do their work with the fear of God in their hearts, so that they would act with all faithfulness (v. 9).

19.5.7.en: 7- The judges must warn the people against transgressing the Law of God, so that they do not trespass against Him, and God's wrath come upon them, especially since Jehoshaphat had experienced the seriousness of sin, which brought God's wrath upon him (v. 2); so he warns his people, that they may not fall as he fell (v. 10).

19.5.8.en: 8- He appointed two to administer these courts, whether in Jerusalem or in the cities of Judah, namely Amariah the priest and Zebadiah the civil ruler, and the priest and the civil ruler are helped by the officers, that is, the Levites who know the Law. Thus he supported the courts with civil authority, alongside the religious authority represented by the priests and the Levites, so that there would be complete discipline in his kingdom.

19.5.9.en: Among the evidences of Jehoshaphat's repentance and return to the Lord is that he repeated the word "the Lord" nine times in these verses (vv. 4-11). We see in these instructions Jehoshaphat's wisdom, his exactness and his organization of the courts, in assigning each person his responsibility, whether civil officials, or priests and Levites, whether in Jerusalem or in all the cities of Judah, and his sound administration and God's support of him appear.

19.5.10.en: Let the word of God be your measure in your conduct. Read the Holy Bible every day and choose a verse to be a message to you from God, to apply in your life. And review yourself at the end of each day by the word of God that you read, and offer repentance for everything in which you sinned, and you will obtain God's mercies and be made worthy to receive the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion.

19.5.11.en: Jehoshaphat's victory over Moab and the children of Ammon

20.0.s.en: (1) Moab and the children of Ammon try to fight Jehoshaphat

20.0.0.en: Moab: they are the offspring of Lot by his elder daughter, and they lived east of the Dead Sea and were at enmity with the people of God for most of their days.

20.0.1.en: The children of Ammon: they are the offspring of Lot by his younger daughter, and they lived north of Moab, east of the Jordan River, and were at enmity with the people of God for most of their days.

20.0.2.en: The Ammonites (Meunim): most likely what is meant is the Ammonites, as in the Jerusalem Bible (the Jesuit translation), and they are some tribes of the Edomites, who lived in Mount Seir; they are the offspring of Esau (Edom), and lived south of the kingdom of Judah. After Jehoshaphat's reforms and his return to God with all his heart and his reforms, Satan stirred up the surrounding nations against him, and God allowed this so that He might be glorified in him, so the Moabites and the children of Ammon, who lived east of the land of the Jews, and likewise the Edomites, who lived south of their land, rose against him; that is, they all united to fight the kingdom of Judah. The reasons for the enemies' attack are not mentioned, and perhaps the reason was their greed for the wealth of the kingdom of Judah.

20.1.0.en: Hazazon-tamar: the ancient name of En-gedi, which lies in the kingdom of Judah, west of the Dead Sea and near it.

20.1.1.en: Jehoshaphat's guards were informed of military movements by the Moabites, the children of Ammon and Edom, and that they had gathered at En-gedi, that is, the south of the kingdom of Judah, and this means that the armies of Moab and the children of Ammon moved to the south of the kingdom of Judah, to unite with the armies of the Edomites and gather for war there.

20.1.2.en: And the word Aram, mentioned here, means Edom, as in the Jesuit translation.

20.1.3.en: Do not be disturbed by the plots of the wicked, for God does not allow them to wrong you except to the extent that you can bear, and He gives you the ability to triumph over them, so that He is glorified in you and you stand firm in your faith.

20.2.0.en: When Jehoshaphat learned of his enemies' preparation to fight him, he was not disturbed but turned to God, as Jehu the son of Hanani had taught him, so he did not try to take refuge in men by allying with them (ch. 19:2); he feared God, therefore he did not fear men, for he felt that the power of God is above every power, and he turned to Him in prayer.

20.2.1.en: Jehoshaphat joined his prayer with fasting, so he proclaimed a fast for all the kingdom of Judah and offered a prayer for his people before God, because the king here represents the whole people.

20.2.2.en: The word of God is clear: that the race of Satan has no strength against prayer and fasting. Therefore in all your afflictions, take refuge in prayer and fasting, to declare your destitution before God and your need of Him alone; then you will find help beyond all imagination, supporting you from God.

20.3.0.en: When the people of the kingdom of Judah learned of the collective fast and prayer, they came to Jerusalem, to the temple of God, to offer prayer and fasting before Him, confident of His promises, which He declared, that against any attack of the enemies, if they lift up their hearts in prayer before Him, He will surely intervene and rescue them (Deut 20:4, 1 Kgs 8:44, 45).

20.4.0.en: The people of the kingdom of Judah gathered in a new court built at the temple, which perhaps Asa, Jehoshaphat's father, prepared or renewed (ch. 15:8), and it may be the great court, that is, the large one, in the temple, and Jehoshaphat stood before them to pray on their behalf before God, that He might rescue them from their enemies.

20.5.0.en: Jehoshaphat began his prayer by glorifying God, who has authority over heaven and earth, and all kingdoms are subject to Him, for He has complete power and no one can resist Him.

20.6.1.en: Jehoshaphat reminds God that He drove out the pagan nations from the land of Canaan and gave their land to His people, the offspring of His friend Abraham; so he reminds God of His care and love for His people, and reminds Him also of His beloved Abraham, interceding by him, that God might have mercy on them and rescue them from their enemies.

20.6.2.en: And he says that God's covenants are firm forever, "I gave them ... forever"; therefore he pleads with Him to intervene, to repel the enemies from them.

20.7.0.en: He reminds God that His people built a temple for Him in the land of Canaan, and that He promised Solomon, when he built this temple, that if the sword of judgment came upon them, that is, an attack by enemies, or any affliction, such as famine and pestilence, He would quickly intervene and rescue His people.

20.8.0.en: The land of Seir: that is, of the Edomites.

20.8.1.en: Jehoshaphat declared to God the seriousness of the attack of a great army from the alliance of Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom, whom God had commanded His people, when entering to possess the land of Canaan, not to attack, but to go around their lands, because they were their cousins (Deut 2:5-7). But sadly these enemies did not keep the kindness of the people of God to them and attacked them to drive them out of their possession; therefore Jehoshaphat asks God to rescue them from these wicked aggressors. And this land, the land of Canaan, God had given to His people, so the attempt of the Moabites and those with them to drive the people of God out of it is a challenge to God and resistance to Him, the giver of the land, and consequently God's intervention is required to rescue His people and establish them in their land.

20.9.0.en: Jehoshaphat specified his petition to God, which was to intervene to rescue His people from their enemies, and he declared to God the following:

20.9.1.en: A- The weakness of his people before the strength of the enemies, that is, his people's great need of God, and it is clear from this that Jehoshaphat did not rely on his many soldiers, who exceeded a million (ch. 17:14-18), but relied on God alone, and we did not hear that Jehoshaphat took care to prepare his armies, but he took care to pray, to obtain God's help.

20.9.2.en: B- He declared that his people's only hope is God, for he said in humility that our eyes are toward You, that is, that You may rescue us.

20.10.0.en: All the people, men, women and children, in the kingdom of Judah were gathered in Jerusalem, hearing the words of Jehoshaphat's prayer with their hearts clinging to God, and because of this humility and taking refuge in God, the Lord intervenes and rescues His people and answers their prayers.

20.11.0.en: God answered Jehoshaphat's prayer quickly, so the Spirit of God came upon one of the Levites, Jahaziel, who called the people and the king and stood in their midst and asked them to listen to the word of God, which he would speak, and gave them the good news that God would lead the war, so they should not fear the enemies because of their number, for they would not fight them, but God would fight them.

20.12.0.en: The cliff of Ziz: a wilderness extending from the west of the Dead Sea to the mountains of Judah.

20.12.1.en: The wilderness of Jeruel: a desert next to the cliff of Ziz.

20.12.2.en: God commanded them, through Jahaziel, that their army should advance the next day to the cliff of Ziz, and they would find the enemies coming up toward them at the far end of this wilderness. Thus the people of God show that they are brave and going down to meet the enemies, though in truth it is God who will fight for them, so their courage is drawn from their faith in God, who answered their prayer and fasting quickly, and commanded them to face the enemies the next day.

20.13.0.en: The Lord reassured them, through Jahaziel, that they would not fight, but would stand with steadfastness and courage to see the Lord who fights for them, and not fear the enemies, because God is with them. And it is clear that they would not take weapons, but would be only spectators of the work of God and His victory, which would be accomplished. And they took with them only singers to praise God, because of their faith that God's word would certainly be carried out.

20.13.1.en: And so we see that whoever fears God and takes refuge in Him with prayer and fasting is not afraid or disturbed by any enemy, because the fear of God drives out the fear of men, and the opposite is true: whoever does not fear God trembles before men.

20.13.2.en: If you are afraid of any problems you are going through, take refuge quickly in God and trust that He is able to reassure you and defend you, so do not be disturbed by threats, or by the strength of the one who tries to wrong you. Believe and be saved.

20.14.0.en: Jehoshaphat and all the people rejoiced at the greatness of the good news, so they all bowed down before the Lord, thanking Him for His love and care, declaring their submission and obedience to all that He had said and their faith in His power, which is able to crush the enemies without their moving or doing anything. Perhaps they remembered God's words to His people in the days of Moses, before their crossing of the Red Sea (Ex 14:13).

20.15.0.en: The people expressed their joy and thanks by the Levites, of the sons of Kohath and the sons of Korah, rising to praise God and thank Him and glorify Him.

20.16.s.en: (4) The victory over Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom

20.16.0.en: The wilderness of Tekoa: it lies southeast of Jerusalem, about 10 km away.

20.16.1.en: The people obeyed and hastened early the next day and went out to meet the enemies at the wilderness of Tekoa, with their king Jehoshaphat, who stood among them, not to prepare them for fighting, like any king or army commander when facing the enemies, but to exhort them and establish them in faith in God, for by Him they obtain reassurance, success and victory in the war, without any effort. And he stressed to them the necessity of believing everything that the prophet of God, Jahaziel, had said.

20.17.0.en: The strange thing about this war is that the army of God advances, not soldiers with experience and military skill, but a group of singers, praising God for His many mercies, as we praise Him today in the Second Hoos, in the praise of the Church.

20.17.1.en: And Jehoshaphat consulted the chiefs of the people, to encourage the army, about having a group of singers go before the army, so that they might lead the people in thanking God and strengthen their faith.

20.18.0.en: Ambushments: plural of ambush, which is a group of soldiers, hidden, who surprise the army by attacking it.

20.18.1.en: When the praise of the people of God began and their faith was established, God intervened in a miraculous way, so ambushes of soldiers moved against the armies of the enemies, and we do not know who the members of these ambushes were; they may have been angels, or the enemies may have disagreed among themselves, so ambushes of them rose against one another, that is, they divided and attacked and destroyed one another.

20.18.2.en: And God did not tell us the kind of the ambushes here, to stress the importance of faith, even if we do not know what exactly God will do.

20.18.3.en: Believe in God however impossible the solution and however complicated the matters, for He is able to save you by means that never occurred to you. Rely on Him, seek Him and let Him do what He sees fit.

20.19.1.en: He tells us here that the armies of the enemies rose against one another, so the Moabites and the Ammonites fought the Edomites and destroyed them, and then the Moabites and the children of Ammon fought one another, so they all perished.

20.20.0.en: The watchtower: the place from which they watch the enemies from afar.

20.20.1.en: The people of God advanced toward the valley in which the enemies had gathered, and found them all dead bodies fallen on the ground, that is, they had all perished.

20.21.s.en: (5) The taking of the spoil and the praise of God

20.21.0.en: King Jehoshaphat and his army advanced toward the dead bodies lying in the valley, and found much spoil of money and precious goods, and they went on gathering it for three days.

20.22.0.en: After the people had gathered the spoil, they assembled in a valley thirteen kilometers south of Bethlehem, and stood praising God and blessing Him, so they called the name of this valley the valley of Berachah, because they blessed God in it.

20.23.0.en: After this, Jehoshaphat and his army returned with great joy to Jerusalem, because God had given them victory over their enemies by His divine power, without their fighting them, and they took much spoil from them.

20.24.0.en: And on entering Jerusalem they hastened to the temple of God, and the procession was led by the singers praising God with musical instruments, such as the psalteries, the harps and the trumpets.

20.24.1.en: Jehoshaphat cared not only for praising God before the battle, but also after God's victory over them and their destroying one another, for thanking God and praising Him is the least we can offer Him after His care and protection of us. Accustom yourself to give thanks in your prayers every day, thanking Him for all that He does with you, whether great things or small.

20.25.0.en: After the destruction of the armies allied against the people of God, the nations heard, so they feared God and His people. And none of them tried to fight the people of God after this, so the kingdom of Judah lived in security and rest in the days of Jehoshaphat, because of their faith and godliness.

20.26.0.en: These verses are recorded and were explained in (1 Kgs 22:42-43), and it shows in them that Jehoshaphat walked with the Lord, like Asa his father, and adds here that the people, despite their faith and godliness, were not perfect in their hearts with God, for they still offered the worship of God on the high places and not in His temple in Jerusalem. And there is a possibility that they offered worship to idols on these high places, as proved by the fact that Jehoshaphat afterwards joined with the wicked Ahaziah, king of Israel, in trade.

20.27.0.en: This verse is recorded and was explained in (1 Kgs 22:45), and we see in it that the acts of Jehoshaphat were written by Jehu the son of Hanani, in a book which is the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah, which is different from the Book of Chronicles in the Holy Bible. From this we understand that Jehu was not only a prophet but also a historian.

20.28.0.en: This incident is recorded in (1 Kgs 22:48), and is mentioned here in detail, as follows:

20.28.1.en: 1- That after God's victory over the enemies of His people, Jehoshaphat sinned by going and joining with a wicked king, Ahaziah king of Israel. And the union was not in war but in trade, so he made ships for trade at Ezion-geber, to go to the cities of the world, the last of which was Tarshish.

20.28.2.en: 2- God sent Eliezer the son of Dodavah the prophet, who rebuked Jehoshaphat for his union with Ahaziah, and prophesied to him that God was angry with him and would attack him. And it actually happened that these ships, which Jehoshaphat had made, were broken.

20.28.3.en: God's mercy appears from this, for He was long-suffering with Jehoshaphat, who sinned by his union with Ahaziah, so He sent him a prophet to rebuke him and his ships were broken, so Jehoshaphat repented, and refused after this to join with Ahaziah in trade, as the Book of Kings tells us (1 Kgs 22:49).

20.28.4.en: Be obedient to God's warnings and rebukes, and even to the afflictions you go through, for they bring you back to God in repentance and you hold fast to His commandments anew.

20.28.5.en: Note: see the life of Jehoshaphat at the end of the book.
